description: We are an ambitious hackathon team from BCIT. We are bringing it home!
summary:
We built an interactive map that finds places on Earth that feel like the Moon and Mars. Our app compares locations using terrain, temperature, geology, water availability, and surface conditions, pulling from both planetary and Earth datasets.

A similarity-scoring algorithm rates how closely each Earth location matches a chosen lunar or Martian site. You can explore the map, check the score for any spot, and see where a comparison holds up and where it falls apart.

Scientists already rely on a handful of well-known analog sites, but there are likely better ones nobody has looked at. By making this data easy to explore, our platform can help researchers and mission planners find overlooked locations, and it gives the public a clearer picture of what other worlds are really like.
details:
Astrolog

Astrolog is an interactive map that finds places on Earth that resemble sites on the Moon and Mars, including ones scientists haven’t studied yet.

How It Works

Astrolog gives you three ways to explore:

  • Scout by operation. Choose what NASA will likely test at these sites, like rover mobility or navigation, and Astrolog finds Earth locations that fit.
  • Start from Earth. Pick any location on Earth and see which lunar and Martian sites it matches best.
  • Compare side by side. Put any two locations next to each other and see exactly how they line up.

You can also filter by layer to opt dimensions in or out of the calculation. Care about terrain but not temperature? Turn temperature off and the score updates.

Astrolog scores every match factor by factor, using methods like Wasserstein distance to compare terrain slope distributions. You see what matches and what doesn’t, not just one number.

What Makes It Different

  • Operations-based exploration. Search by what NASA will actually do, like rover mobility and navigation, not just by how a place looks.
  • No single score. We break each match into separate factors. A spot might match Mars in terrain but not temperature, and we show you both.
  • Discovery over documentation. Instead of listing known analog sites like Antarctica, the Atacama, and Iceland, Astrolog finds new ones computationally.

Why It Matters

  • Research: Surfaces overlooked Earth locations worth investigating.
  • Mission planning: Gives early environmental comparisons for lunar and Martian exploration.
  • Education: Makes planetary data easy for students and the public to explore.

Limitations

No place on Earth can copy lunar gravity, the Moon’s vacuum, Martian air pressure, or radiation. Datasets also vary in resolution and coverage. Astrolog is a discovery and comparison tool, not a certifier of analog sites.
dataRefs: LRO datasets — LOLA terrain, Diviner temperature and rock abundance, LROC imagery, DEMs and pits, LAMP, LEND
Lunar polar terrain and illumination models
Mars Global Surveyor datasets — MOLA elevation, TES thermal inertia, albedo and dust cover
Mars Odyssey datasets — THEMIS temperature and thermal inertia, GRS and neutron measurements
Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter datasets — CTX, HiRISE, CRISM, SHARAD, MCS and MARC
USGS planetary maps — HRSC–MOLA blended DEM, lunar NAC DEM, Mars geology and cave catalog
MODIS Earth datasets — surface temperature and vegetation indices
Mars surface mission measurements — Curiosity REMS/RAD and Phoenix chemistry
Apollo experiment records — LEAM and CCIG
